title: Pitch-controlled reorientational nonlinearity in chiral nematic liquid crystals: a reduced-order model for self-focusing and soliton formation
authors: Homa Saadatmand, M. Javad Zakeri, Ahmed Sameh Ahmed, Suraj Bhandari, Loubna Benkoula, Ameer B. Batarseh, Andrea Blanco-Redondo, Miroslaw Karpierz, Pawel S. Jung
abstract: We present a reduced-order semi-analytical model for reorientational nonlinearity in chiral nematic liquid crystals, showing that the chiral pitch acts as the dominant physical length scale governing the onset of nonlinear self-focusing and soliton formation. Starting from the full Frank-Oseen equation, we derive a closed-form expression for the optically induced molecular rotation that captures the essential saturable response of the medium while reducing computational cost by more than two orders of magnitude compared with standard relaxation-method solvers. Despite its simplicity, the model reproduces the essential features of the numerically obtained nonlinear refractive index, the onset of self-localization, and the transition from discrete to continuous solitons in one and two dimensions. It further predicts the formation of fully localized astigmatic nematicons with only minor shifts in the self-localization threshold due to the neglect of nonlocal effects. The proposed model provides direct physical insight into light-matter interactions with soft matter media and offers a computationally efficient tool for the design and optimization of nonlinear photonic devices.
summary: This work presents a highly efficient, reduced-order model for analyzing how light interacts with chiral nematic liquid crystals. It successfully predicts the formation of optical solitons and self-focusing, demonstrating that the crystal's inherent chiral pitch dictates the confinement scale. This provides a powerful, fast tool for designing nonlinear photonic devices using soft matter.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a computationally efficient model to study nonlinear self-focusing and soliton formation in chiral nematic liquid crystals (ChNLCs).
main_result: The reduced-order model successfully reproduces the essential physics of saturable reorientational self-focusing, showing that the chiral pitch governs the characteristic length scale for soliton formation.
method: The authors derived a reduced-order, semi-analytical model starting from the full Frank-Oseen equation, significantly reducing computational cost compared to standard iterative solvers.
model_or_system: The system is Chiral Nematic Liquid Crystals (ChNLCs) whose optical properties are governed by light-induced molecular reorientation, described by the Frank-Oseen free energy minimization.
key_observables: Nonlinear refractive index, onset of self-localization, formation of discrete/continuous solitons, and astigmatic nematicons.
important_parameters: Chiral Pitch (Lambda, $\Lambda$), input beam waist ($\omega_0$), and elastic constants ($K$).
main_assumptions: The model employs an adiabatic approximation for director dynamics and neglects full spatial nonlocality and long-range elastic interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ChNLC cell structure, beam propagation, index modulation, and 2D soliton intensity distributions comparing exact and simplified model predictions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical problem and governing equations (Frank-Oseen) to deriving the reduced-order model, validating its ability to capture key nonlinear phenomena (self-focusing, soliton transition) across 1D and 2D geometries.
why_interesting: The coupling between light propagation (optics) and the nonlinear, soft-matter director field (liquid crystals) presents a complex, non-Hamiltonian, nonlinear wave problem relevant to nonlinear optics and pattern formation.
